title: Unconditional Modified Regev Factoring
statement: Unconditional nontrivial-divisor algorithm with modified randomized base selection.

target.description: Any composite $N\le 2^n$; even integers and prime powers are handled by classical preliminary steps.

assumptions: The algorithm samples small primes together with one uniform element of $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^\times$; it is not Regev's original fixed-small-prime construction.

time.note: No total bound is extracted for this coordinate in the checked result.

memory.note: No total classical/quantum memory bound is extracted for this result.

classical_time.note: Randomized classical sampling and lattice postprocessing; excludes the quantum calls.

quantum_calls.note: Total calls to the circuit in Theorem 1.1.

gates_per_call.note: Algorithmic per-call circuit bound in Theorem 1.1; not a total runtime.

logical_qubits.note: Theorem 1.1 statement; the unproved-in-this-paper logarithmic refinement in Remark 1.3 is not substituted.

success.description: Theorem 1.1 and its proof establish constant overall probability, including the randomized base selection.

review.scope: Checked the stated event and bound in the cited theorem/corollary and its surrounding argument; not a proof reproduction.

evidence.locator: PDF/printed p. 2, Theorem 1.1; pp. 5–6, Section 1.4; p. 23, proof of Theorem 1.1.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted transcription of this result's input, output, cost accounting and success event; not a full-paper audit.

limitations: Does not remove the hypothesis for the original deterministic first-small-primes choice; see Section 1.4 and Remark 1.6.
Discrete-logarithm results from the same paper are not included in this factorization batch.
